title: All-Time Great Indian Horror Films
description: 25 films that shaped Indian horror through ghosts, folklore, psychological terror, mythology and supernatural dread.
intro: The top five represent five different strengths of Indian horror: psychological classic, folk horror, pure supernatural fear, slow-burn psychological horror, and modern folklore horror.

entries.why_it_ranks: The complete package — psychological horror, supernatural atmosphere, mystery, folklore, comedy, extraordinary performances and enormous influence across Indian cinema.
Probably India's greatest folk-horror achievement visually. Mythology, greed and dread combine into something unlike almost anything else in Indian cinema.
Ram Gopal Varma understands that silence, darkness and anticipation can be far more frightening than constant jump scares.
One of India's most psychologically unsettling horror films. Grief and supernatural terror gradually become almost impossible to separate.
Mammootty, monochrome cinematography, folklore and an oppressive sense of power create an exceptional modern folk-horror experience.
Cleverly constructed and enormously influential on later South Indian horror. It constantly manipulates what the viewer believes is happening.
A television serial apparently predicting a family's future remains one of Indian horror cinema's smartest central concepts.
Anushka Shetty, Sonu Sood and grand supernatural mythology turned this into one of Telugu cinema's defining horror-fantasy films.
Historically indispensable. Kamal Amrohi helped establish the haunted-mansion, reincarnation and gothic-romance vocabulary that Indian supernatural cinema repeatedly returned to.
One of India's strongest straight supernatural-horror films, particularly effective in sound design, atmosphere and possession sequences.
A surprisingly grounded possession film that builds fear patiently and gives its supernatural threat genuine weight.
Nayanthara leads an atmospheric, carefully structured supernatural mystery that relies more on mood than cheap shocks.
Rural isolation, superstition and social horror combine into something genuinely disturbing.
An unusual supernatural murder mystery that uses water as its central horror motif remarkably effectively.
Anushka Sharma's dark supernatural drama takes its mythology seriously and avoids the usual Bollywood haunted-house formula.
Jewish folklore gives this possession story a distinctive identity within Indian supernatural cinema.
Occult practices, village mythology and an escalating mystery make it one of Telugu cinema's strongest recent horror films.
RGV turns an ordinary Mumbai apartment into an intensely claustrophobic haunted space, with Urmila Matondkar giving a memorable performance.
Mysskin combines ghost-story conventions with grief and compassion, creating a supernatural film with an unusually emotional centre.
Economical, creepy and effective. The haunted-location premise becomes increasingly claustrophobic as the film progresses.
Not the most sophisticated entry here, but historically important to the revival of mainstream Hindi horror in the early 2000s and still highly memorable.
Psychological trauma, home invasion and videogame-style structure combine into a tense genre experiment.
Not conventional ghost horror at all. It gradually turns desire, food and obsession into deeply uncomfortable body horror.
Horror-comedy done unusually well, combining folklore, scares, humour and social commentary without completely neutralizing its monster.
An important atmospheric Telugu horror film from RGV's strongest filmmaking period.
